The Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A) is a small USB-C and UART interface board that powers and controls Feetech ST/SC-series bus servos (STS3215, STS3250) from a PC, Raspberry Pi or microcontroller, and is the board most LeRobot SO-101 and LeKiwi builds use in place of the BusLinker V3.0. One board drives one servo chain, so a leader-and-follower SO-ARM101 pair needs two — which is how they are packed here.The Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A) is the low-cost USB interface most LeRobot builders use to drive Feetech STS3215 servos from a laptop or Raspberry Pi. Plug in 12 V, connect the servo chain, and the board appears as a serial port for LeRobot, the Waveshare servo tool or your own Python code. A direct alternative to the BusLinker V3.0 for SO-ARM101 and LeKiwi builds.What can you use it for? Controller for a self-built SO-ARM100 / SO-ARM101 leader or follower arm Setting servo IDs and offsets before assembly LeKiwi mobile base and OpenDuck Mini servo bus Any Feetech-servo robot driven from Python, ESP32 or Arduino Who is it for?Builders assembling SO-101 arms from servos and printed parts, and anyone who needs a spare or second USB servo interface.Compatibility Servos: Feetech STS3215, STS3250, STS3235, SCS series Hosts: Windows, macOS, Linux, Raspberry Pi (USB serial); ESP32 / Arduino / STM32 via UART Software: Hugging Face LeRobot (feetech motor bus), Waveshare servo tool, Feetech SDK Power: Waveshare rates the DC input at 9–12.6 V; it is passed straight to the servos, so the supply must match them — use 12 V 5 A for six STS3215-C018 Specifications Model Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A) Servo protocol Feetech ST / SC series half-duplex TTL bus (STS3215, STS3250, SCS series) Host interface USB-C (CH343 serial) or 3-pin UART header (TX / RX / GND), selectable by jumper Servo ports 2 × 3-pin servo headers; daisy-chain up to 253 servos Power input DC 9–12.6 V rated (Waveshare specification), passed through to the servo bus, via 5.5 × 2.1 mm barrel jack or screw terminal Onboard Power switch circuitry, PWR LED, brass standoffs Software LeRobot Feetech motor bus, Waveshare bus servo tool, Python SDK, Arduino / ESP32 / Raspberry Pi examples Size About 40 × 30 mm Ships from Singapore, with tracking What's in the box 2 boards — one leader and one follower arm: 2 × Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A) with brass standoffs — one per arm of an SO-ARM101 pair (no cables or power supply) 4 boards — bimanual rig or class bench: 4 × Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A) with brass standoffs — two arm pairs, or four student benches (no cables or power supply) 1 board — single arm or bus: 1 × Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A) with brass standoffs (no cables or power supply) Shipping and returnsShips from Singapore with tracking, charged by parcel weight and shown in full before payment. A standard SO-ARM101 build is a leader arm and a follower arm on separate buses, so it needs two — that is the default pack. A LeKiwi base or a single arm needs one; a bimanual rig or a classroom with four benches needs four. Two boards weigh 80 g, the same postage band as one.Is this the same as the BusLinker V3.0?Functionally yes: both turn USB into the Feetech servo bus and pass DC power to the servos. LeRobot works with either.Can it power the servos from USB?No. USB only powers the logic. Servos take power from the barrel jack or screw terminal, so connect a supply that matches the servos: 12 V for STS3215-C018 and STS3250, 7.4 V for the 7.4 V STS3215 models in an SO-101 leader arm. Waveshare's own rating for the input is 9–12.6 V.How many servos can I chain?Up to 253 addresses on one bus; in practice six per arm, limited by the power supply, not the board. Complete the build Pair this board with Feetech STS3215 servos, 3-pin cables, and power (12 V 5 A or the dual-voltage kit). One SO-ARM101 arm needs 6 servos on one board; leader+follower needs 12 servos and two boards. Fastest start: STS3215 Starter Kit.

The Feetech FE-URT-2 (URT-2) is Feetech's USB-C to TTL and RS485 converter for its own bus servos: it connects HD-1910, STS3215, SCS-series and RS485 SMS-series servos to a computer so that Feetech's software can set each servo's ID, baud rate and limits, test motion and read back position before the servos are built into a robot.This is the current URT-2 revision with a USB-C port, and a USB-A to USB-C data cable is in the box. Plug the board into a computer and set up one servo at a time: for setting IDs and parameters USB alone powers the servo port, and an external supply on the screw terminal runs servos under load. It is the board Feetech pairs with the HD-1910 for Microduck-style builds, and the tool you need to give fifteen identical servos their fifteen different IDs before assembly.What can you use it for? Replacing or upgrading a joint in an SO-ARM100 / SO-ARM101 leader or follower arm Building an SO-101 arm from printed parts: the 12-servo set matches the official bill of materials LeKiwi mobile base (3 × 12 V wheel servos) or the full LeKiwi robot (base + arm) OpenDuck Mini bipedal robot (14 × 7.4 V servos) 12-DOF robot dogs and quadrupeds, three servos per leg: the robot dog set has 12 × 12 V C018 (30 kg·cm) for the leg joints Custom robots, grippers and pan-tilt heads that need position, load and temperature feedback over one bus Who is it for?LeRobot builders sourcing exact-spec servos, robot-dog and quadruped builders, robotics students, and makers who want feedback servos that are cheaper than Dynamixel but supported by open-source software.Compatibility Controllers: BusLinker V3.0, Waveshare bus servo adapter, Feetech FE-URT-2, or any 3.3 V / 5 V UART with half-duplex direction control Software: Hugging Face LeRobot (feetech motor bus), Feetech FD software, Python (scservo_sdk), Arduino and ESP32 libraries Horns: 25 T spline, metal horns included; compatible with SO-101 and LeKiwi printed parts Voltage: C018 runs on 12 V (SO-101 follower joints); C001 / C044 / C046 run on 7.4 V (leader arm and light joints) — do not feed 12 V to the 7.4 V models Specifications Model Feetech STS3215 (ST3215) smart serial bus servo Stall torque C018: 30 kg·cm at 12 V; C001 / C044 / C046: 19 kg·cm at 7.4 V (1:345), lower on the faster ratios Gear ratio 1:345 (C018, C001), 1:191 (C044), 1:147 (C046) Speed 0.16 s/60° (C018 at 12 V); 52 rpm at 7.4 V for 1:345 models Position sensor 12-bit magnetic encoder, 4096 steps over 360°, 0.088° resolution Control modes Position (0–360°), constant-speed wheel, open-loop PWM, step mode, multi-turn absolute position Interface Half-duplex TTL serial bus, 38 400 bps – 1 Mbps, daisy-chain up to 253 IDs, 3-pin cable Feedback Position, speed, load, voltage, temperature, current, moving status; over-current and over-temperature protection Voltage C018: 6–12.6 V (use 12 V); C001: 4–7.4 V, over-voltage protection above 8 V; C044 / C046: 5–8.4 V. Power a mixed leader arm from 5 V (LeRobot's guide) or 7.4 V, not 8.4 V Gears Metal (brass and steel), dual-shaft housing with rear bearing, 25 T spline Size / weight 45.2 × 24.7 × 35 mm, 55 g Free shipping: orders of $100 or more ship free when the shipping charge is $22.99 or less (most destinations outside the US). Die 12-V-Version C018 (30 kg·cm) für den Follower-Arm, die 7,4-V-Versionen C001/C044/C046 mit unterschiedlichen Übersetzungen für den Leader-Arm; dazu fertige Sets für SO-ARM101, LeKiwi und OpenDuck Mini. Versand mit Sendungsverfolgung aus Singapur, Preise in Euro, Bezahlung auch per PayPal. Einfuhrabgaben, falls erhoben, trägt der Empfänger. Fragen gern auf Deutsch an info@armdojo.com.Frequently asked questionsWhich STS3215 do I need for the SO-ARM101?The follower arm uses six 12 V C018 (30 kg·cm) servos. The leader arm uses 7.4 V servos with three different gear ratios so it is light to move by hand: the 12-servo set on this page contains exactly the mix from the SO-101 bill of materials.What is the difference between C018, C001, C044 and C046?C018 is the 12 V, 30 kg·cm, 1:345 version. C001 is the 7.4 V, 19 kg·cm, 1:345 version. C044 (1:191) and C046 (1:147) are 7.4 V servos with lower gear ratios: faster and easier to back-drive, less torque; the SO-101 leader arm uses them for the joints you move most.Is it a real Feetech servo?Yes. These are genuine Feetech STS3215 servos with the Feetech label, magnetic encoder and metal gearbox, the same part sold by Seeed and Waveshare.Can I control it from Arduino or Raspberry Pi?Yes. It speaks the Feetech half-duplex serial protocol. Use a bus servo board such as the BusLinker V3.0 or a Waveshare adapter for USB, or a UART plus direction pin on a microcontroller with the Feetech SCServo library.Does it do continuous rotation?Yes. Besides 0–360° position mode it supports wheel (constant speed) mode, open-loop PWM mode, step mode and multi-turn absolute position, selectable by register.What power supply do I need?12 V 5 A for six C018 servos in an arm; 7.4 V (2S LiPo or a 7.4 V supply) for the C001 / C044 / C046 models. Each servo draws about 0.9 A rated and up to 2–3 A at stall. Complete the build One SO-ARM101 arm needs 6 STS3215 servos; a leader+follower pair needs 12. Recommended path: single servo → Waveshare adapter → cables → dual-voltage power → 6/12 kit / starter. Also see metal horns.Build guides Free Online Servo ID Tool: number your servos one by one in Chrome or Edge with the FE-URT-2, check the chain and center a servo, nothing to install Feetech servo setup guide: set the voltage, wire the FE-URT-2 and give every servo its own ID, with diagrams and a printable PDF STS3215 robot dog parts list: what a 12-DOF quadruped needs: servo version, controller, power and open-source frames SO-101 bill of materials and real cost: every part of a leader and follower pair Powering 12 V vs 7.4 V servos: adapters, current and wiring Setting STS3215 servo IDs and zero offsets: the setup every build starts with Robot Builder FAQ: which servo for which robot, SO-101, Open Duck, robot dogs and ordering

Fragen gern auf Deutsch an info@armdojo.com.Frequently asked questionsWhich STS3215 do I need for the SO-ARM101?The follower arm uses six 12 V C018 (30 kg·cm) servos. The leader arm uses 7.4 V servos with three different gear ratios so it is light to move by hand: the 12-servo set on this page contains exactly the mix from the SO-101 bill of materials.What is the difference between C018, C001, C044 and C046?C018 is the 12 V, 30 kg·cm, 1:345 version. C001 is the 7.4 V, 19 kg·cm, 1:345 version. C044 (1:191) and C046 (1:147) are 7.4 V servos with lower gear ratios: faster and easier to back-drive, less torque; the SO-101 leader arm uses them for the joints you move most.Is it a real Feetech servo?Yes. These are genuine Feetech STS3215 servos with the Feetech label, magnetic encoder and metal gearbox, the same part sold by Seeed and Waveshare.Can I control it from Arduino or Raspberry Pi?Yes. It speaks the Feetech half-duplex serial protocol. Use a bus servo board such as the BusLinker V3.0 or a Waveshare adapter for USB, or a UART plus direction pin on a microcontroller with the Feetech SCServo library.Does it do continuous rotation?Yes. Besides 0–360° position mode it supports wheel (constant speed) mode, open-loop PWM mode, step mode and multi-turn absolute position, selectable by register.What power supply do I need?12 V 5 A for six C018 servos in an arm; 7.4 V (2S LiPo or a 7.4 V supply) for the C001 / C044 / C046 models. Each servo draws about 0.9 A rated and up to 2–3 A at stall. Complete the build One SO-ARM101 arm needs 6 STS3215 servos; a leader+follower pair needs 12. The Feetech HD-1910-C001 is a 21 g coreless-motor serial bus servo with a metal gearbox, a 360° magnetic encoder and a dual-shaft output, delivering 12 kg·cm of stall torque at 6 V in a 34 × 20 × 23 mm body; Feetech released it in September 2026 as the actuator for community builds of Microduck-style biped robots, which use fifteen of them — one per joint.The HD-1910-C001 is Feetech's small coreless-motor bus servo, released in September 2026 for Microduck-style biped robots: 12 kg·cm stall torque at 6 V in a 34 × 20 × 23 mm, 21 g body, with a 360° magnetic encoder and a dual-shaft output for bracket-mounted joints. Fifteen of them drive one robot, so the 15-servo set is the default pack; it weighs about 480 g packed. In stock: ships from our Singapore warehouse within 1–2 business days, with tracked shipping.What can you use it for? Community builds of the Microduck 25 cm biped (legs, neck and beak): fifteen servos per robot Small bipeds, quadrupeds and robot pets where a 60 g STS3215 is too big Compact grippers, pan-tilt heads and desktop companion robots Replacing a damaged joint servo in an HD-1910 build Who is it for?Makers building Microduck-style or other small legged robots who want position-feedback bus servos at a fraction of the size of an STS3215, and are comfortable configuring servo IDs themselves.Compatibility Protocol: Feetech half-duplex TTL serial bus; configure with the FE-URT-2 debug board and Feetech's software or the Feetech SCServo SDK Power: 4–8.4 V; a 2S LiPo is 8.4 V when full, the top of the range; a regulated 6–7.4 V supply is the safe choice Official Microduck: it ships with Dynamixel XL330 servos and firmware for Dynamixel. A standard SO-ARM101 build is a leader arm and a follower arm on separate buses, so it needs two — that is the default pack. A spare, a single arm or a LeKiwi base needs one; a bimanual rig or a four-bench classroom needs four. Two boards weigh 80 g, the same postage band as one.Is this the board inside the SO-ARM101?Yes. Each SO-ARM101 arm has one BusLinker V3.0 in its base connecting the six servos to the PC. This listing is the bare board for spares, second arms or custom builds.How do I connect it?USB-C to the computer, 12 V into the barrel jack or screw terminal, and the servo chain into any of the three 3-pin ports. The board appears as a serial port; select it in LeRobot or the PC servo tool.Can it power the servos?Yes. The DC input feeds the servo bus directly, so choose an adapter matched to your servos: 12 V for HX-30HM / STS3215-C018, 7.4 V for the 7.4 V models. USB alone does not power servos.Does it work with Feetech STS3215 servos and LeRobot?Yes. The protocol is the same Feetech half-duplex bus that LeRobot's motor driver uses; set the port in your robot config and it works like any other Feetech adapter.Can I use it without a computer?Yes. The 4-pin TTL header (5 V, GND, TX, RX) lets an Arduino, ESP32 or STM32 drive the bus. Sample code for each platform is provided.
